answer.rationale: Full switch to the low-cost vendor is the only option that meets the 18% mandate alone, but doing it as a rip-and-replace 14 days before expiry with the line at 94% and no buffer directly increases delivery risk, violating the primary objective. Renewing or renegotiating with the incumbent is blocked on price (they refused to reopen), and deferral is unsafe because the contract does not auto-renew. The risk-compatible single move is to qualify the low-cost vendor as a second source now: it preserves incumbent continuity for the constrained line (c1), uses the low-cost vendor's demonstrated onboarding/invoicing capability (c2), and replicates the dual-source allocation resilience that held through a prior shortage (c3), while creating competitive leverage and a staged path to shift volume and capture the mandate without betting the line on an unbuffered migration. I am verifying c3 because the whole hedge depends on second-sourcing actually protecting allocation under constraint.
